run_metadata.coverage_summary: Discovery was performed via web search only. As in recent runs, this session's network policy blocks the direct page-fetch tools: WebFetch returns getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for every non-allowlisted host (tender portals, buyer sites, aggregators all fail) and the egress proxy only permits package registries, GitHub and Anthropic endpoints, so no tender detail page, portal listing, or specification document could be opened directly. All findings come from search-engine result summaries. The live JS-rendered government portals (AusTender, NSW eTendering, Buying for Victoria, QTenders, Tenders WA/SA/TAS/ACT) could not be read directly, and the general search index lags the last-7-days window by months, so the overwhelming majority of surfaced opportunities were mid-2026 and already closed (discarded). Two genuinely current, buyer-originated opportunities were confirmed from the buyer's own site or an official DFAT business notification and are reported at headline level with the scope that is publicly stated (no document-level extraction was possible). Tier 3 (private sector) was queried (SAP Business Network Discovery, EstimateOne, SAP Ariba supplier portals for Woolworths/Coles/BHP/Rio/Fortescue, Qantas Coupa) but no publicly-visible corporate RFx was found: those channels are registration- or invitation-gated, so only the portals are recorded in discovered_sources, never invented as tenders. Source discovery surfaced one new buyer-originated portal (ACT Suburban Land Agency) and one new aggregator (projectory.com.au, discovery-signal only).
gaps: WebFetch tool non-functional in this environment: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for every tender host (www.tenders.gov.au, tenders.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders, vendorpanel.com.au, suburbanland.act.gov.au, ausconnect.dfat.gov.au, service.ariba.com, etc.). The session egress proxy allowlist covers only package registries, GitHub and Anthropic endpoints, so no detail page or document could be fetched. These hosts must be added to the session's network settings for an authenticated/unblocked detail pass.

As a result, deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, documents, contacts and exact values could NOT be extracted from the notices or their documents for any opportunity. The two reported tenders carry only the scope that was publicly stated in search summaries of the buyer's own site / official notice, and both need a future document-level detail pass (counted in entries_pending_detail).
Tier 1 AusTender (Commonwealth): no specific current open ATM could be confirmed from the buyer's portal; search returned only guidance pages and stale/aggregator listings. Not exhaustively covered.

Tier 1 NSW eTendering, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/supply.qld.gov.au, Tenders WA, Tenders SA, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL: search returned only stale (mid-2026, already-closed) or aggregator data; no current open tender could be confirmed from the buyer's own portal this run.

Discovery signal NOT confirmed to buyer source (excluded from tenders to avoid aggregator-only reliance): Department of Defence Project LAND 6504 ground-based medium-range air-defence capability tender, reported opened 13 Oct 2026 via the Govly aggregator only; could not be verified on AusTender (host blocked). Recorded here as a lead for a future verified run.

Discovery signals seen only via aggregators and NOT included as tenders: 'ETP Sludge Dewatering Upgrade - EOI' (Melbourne Water, via australiantenders/bidsfactory), SA Water physical/electronic security tender (via sen.news), Sydney Water biosolids/odour-control panels (all appeared already closed in summaries). Pivot to each utility's own supplier portal on a future unblocked run.

Tier 3 private sector: SAP Business Network Discovery, Coupa, EstimateOne, and SAP Ariba supplier portals for Woolworths, Coles, BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue, Qantas were queried but all individual opportunities are login/registration-gated or invitation-only; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was discoverable. Portals recorded only, per spec. Management-consultancy RFPs remain invitation-only and out of scope.

ACT Suburban Land Agency Kingston opportunity: the exact land parcel designation differs across sources ('Block AAb Section 49' on the ACT tenders portal vs 'Block b Section 49 / Kingston Quarter' on the SLA project page and property listings); captured with that caveat. Closing date (1 Dec 2026) is confirmed via the SLA/news deadline-extension announcement but the official notice page itself could not be opened.

DFAT Timor-Leste LMSSP (DFAT-1064): DFAT's own notification states an anticipated Q3 2026 approach to market (RFEOI, two-step). As of this run (late Oct / Q4 2026) it was not confirmed whether the RFEOI is live on AusTender/AusConnect; recorded as a market-sounding/forecast notice at headline level. A DevelopmentAid mirror showed a conflicting 'Q1 2026/2027, Forecast' status and reference 'DFA-1064'.
recommended_seed_additions: ACT Suburban Land Agency (suburbanland.act.gov.au) — ACT territory land development agency that runs design-based tenders / land-release RFTs for major urban renewal sites (e.g. Kingston Arts Precinct); buyer-originated, publishes via the ACT Government tenders portal. Worth adding to the permanent known-source list (gov-state, high confidence).

projectory.com.au — Australian tender aggregator with per-state 'new this week' category pages and an RSS feed (projectory.com.au/rss.xml). Aggregator/reseller, NOT a source of truth; keep only as a low-confidence discovery signal to spot buyers/portals, then pivot to the buyer's own source.

tenders.dedup_key: Tenders ACT:Kingston Section 49 Design Based Tender (Kingston Quarter + Arts Precinct Stage 1)
tenders.source_name: ACT Government Tenders (tenders.act.gov.au) / Suburban Land Agency
tenders.tender_id: Kingston Section 49 (Block AAb) Design Based Tender
tenders.title: Kingston Section 49 Design Based Tender — Kingston Quarter land release & Kingston Arts Precinct (Stage 1)
tenders.category: Property development / urban renewal (design-based land sale)
tenders.description: The ACT Suburban Land Agency is offering the first stage of the Kingston Section 49 renewal site for sale to developers by Design Based Tender. The site comprises a land-release block ('The Kingston Quarter', ~21,360m2, potential for up to ~250 dwellings) and a separate block for the future Kingston Arts Precinct. The submission deadline was extended from 20 October to 1 December 2026 (announced 8 October 2026).
tenders.deliverables_summary: The successful respondent purchases and develops the Kingston Section 49 site under a design-based tender, delivering a mixed-use urban renewal outcome: a residential land-release component ('Kingston Quarter', ~21,360m2, up to ~250 dwellings) and the delivery/enablement of the adjoining future Kingston Arts Precinct in accordance with the SLA's design and sale conditions. Full deliverables, design requirements and sale conditions are in the tender documents, which could not be opened in this environment.
key_deliverables: Purchase and development of the Kingston Quarter land-release block (~21,360m2, up to ~250 dwellings)
Design-led development response for the Kingston Section 49 site
Delivery / enablement of the Stage 1 Kingston Arts Precinct block (per SLA conditions)
tenders.scope_of_work: Design Based Tender sale of the Kingston Section 49 site by the Suburban Land Agency. Public reporting notes the overall site includes 'The Kingston Quarter' land-release block (~21,360m2, capacity for up to ~250 dwellings) plus a block reserved for the future Kingston Arts Precinct. Detailed scope, prescribed design/sale conditions and evaluation requirements are set out in the tender documents (not accessible this run).
tenders.eligibility: Open to developers responding to the design-based tender (full eligibility conditions in the tender documents, not accessible this run).
tenders.submission_method: Lodge via the ACT Government tenders portal (tenders.act.gov.au)
tenders.detail_source: Search-result summaries of the Suburban Land Agency Kingston project-updates page (suburbanland.act.gov.au/our-places/kingston/project-updates) and region.com.au reporting of the deadline extension (8 Oct 2026) to 1 Dec 2026; the official ACT tenders notice page could not be opened directly (WebFetch host blocked).
tenders.reasoning: Surfaced via a forward-dated-closing web search ('closing December 2026'); the ACT tenders portal listing (closing 1 Dec 2026) was corroborated by the Suburban Land Agency's own project-update page and by region.com.au's report that the SLA extended the Kingston Arts Precinct tender deadline from 20 Oct to 1 Dec 2026. Buyer-originated (ACT Government / Suburban Land Agency).
tenders.notes: Parcel designation differs across sources ('Block AAb Section 49' on the ACT tenders portal vs 'Block b Section 49 / Kingston Quarter' on the SLA/property pages) — treat as the same Kingston Section 49 design-based tender. publish_date (30 Jun 2026) and closing_date (1 Dec 2026) taken from search summaries; the tender documents, exact closing time, evaluation criteria, value and contacts need a document-level pass once portal hosts are unblocked. Headline-level entry.

tenders.dedup_key: DFAT AusConnect:DFAT-1064 Timor-Leste Labour Mobility and Skills Support Program
tenders.source_name: DFAT — Business Notifications / Development Procurement Pipeline (AusConnect)
tenders.jurisdiction: Commonwealth of Australia (DFAT) — program delivered in Timor-Leste
tenders.title: Timor-Leste Labour Mobility and Skills Support Program (LMSSP) — Managing Contractor (upcoming RFEOI)
tenders.buyer: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
tenders.category: Development / managing-contractor services; labour mobility & skills; infrastructure
tenders.description: DFAT has notified industry of an upcoming procurement for a managing contractor to implement the Timor-Leste Labour Mobility and Skills Support Program (LMSSP). DFAT anticipated approaching the market with a Request for Expressions of Interest (RFEOI) as the first stage of a two-step (RFEOI then RFT) process; firms that do not respond to the RFEOI will not be invited to the subsequent RFT.
tenders.deliverables_summary: A managing contractor to implement the LMSSP in Timor-Leste: coordinating technical and strategic partnerships, managing infrastructure delivery (expected to include the design and construction of a Labour Mobility Centre in Dili), administering grants/partnership mechanisms as required, and delivering monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting (MEL) services. Full scope and requirements will be in the RFEOI/RFT documents, not yet accessible.
key_deliverables: Implement the Labour Mobility and Skills Support Program (LMSSP) as managing contractor
Manage infrastructure delivery, incl. design & construction of a Labour Mobility Centre in Dili
Administer grants / partnership mechanisms as required
Deliver monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting (MEL) services
tenders.scope_of_work: Per DFAT's business notification: DFAT intends to procure a managing contractor for its flagship labour mobility and skills program in Timor-Leste, responsible for implementation including partnership coordination, infrastructure delivery (expected to include a Dili Labour Mobility Centre), grant/partnership administration, and MEL. Two-step procurement: RFEOI first stage (anticipated Q3 2026), then RFT for invited respondents.
tenders.eligibility: Open to industry at the RFEOI stage; only RFEOI respondents will be invited to the subsequent RFT (two-step process).
tenders.submission_method: Respond to the RFEOI once published (expected via AusTender / DFAT AusConnect); monitor the DFAT Development Procurement Pipeline for status.
tenders.delivery_location: Timor-Leste (program), incl. Dili (Labour Mobility Centre); procured by DFAT (Canberra)
tenders.detail_source: Search-result summary of DFAT's own business notification page (dfat.gov.au/about-us/business-opportunities/business-notifications/labour-mobility-and-skills-program); the page and the Development Procurement Pipeline could not be opened directly (WebFetch host blocked).
tenders.reasoning: Surfaced via a procurement-news/pipeline web search; DFAT's own business notification describes the upcoming LMSSP managing-contractor procurement and two-step RFEOI→RFT process. Buyer-originated (DFAT). Recorded as a market-sounding / upcoming-procurement notice because it was not confirmed this run whether the RFEOI is live.
tenders.notes: DFAT's notification anticipated a Q3 2026 approach to market; as of this run (late Oct / Q4 2026) it was not confirmed whether the RFEOI is live on AusTender/AusConnect (hosts blocked) — closing_date/publish_date left null to avoid fabrication. Bilateral funding context: ~A$48.6m Timor-Leste-Australia Labour Mobility and Skills Partnership (Dec 2024 joint statement) — this is partnership funding, NOT a stated contract value. A DevelopmentAid mirror showed a conflicting reference 'DFA-1064' and 'Q1 2026/2027, Forecast'. Headline-level entry; RFEOI documents need a future pass.
